messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — I ran a geo latency sweep for the newly onboarded quantized Llama-2-13B-qlora (int8) across A100/H100 in us-east1 / us-west2 / eu-west1. Edge routing ON. p50s look fine (~90–150ms) but us-west p95 is high: ~720ms vs us-east ~220ms. Posting bench summary + command. cc @jorge @kevin

benchbot: AUTO-BENCH REPORT (1769876544)
model=llama-2-13b-qlora-int8, seq=512, batch=4, kernels=auto
Results (p50 / p95 / std):
- us-east1 (A100): 120ms / 220ms / 18ms
- us-west2 (A100): 130ms / 720ms / 65ms  <-- tail latency spike
- eu-west1 (H100): 95ms / 210ms / 22ms
Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcdef/geo-latency
Logs: s3://redwood-logs/bench/1769876543.log

Command used:
```bash
./bench_runner.py --model llama-2-13b-qlora --quant int8 --seq 512 --batch 4 --warmup 20 --kernel auto --regions us-east1,us-west2,eu-west1
```

jorge: Did you pin kernel builds? My guess is us-west fell back to the generic attention kernel (no fused path) due to a driver/kernel mismatch :thinking:

maya: I left kernel=auto for this run to capture real-world routing behavior. Full config snippet below (quick):
```json
{"kernel":"auto","quant":"int8","batch":4,"seq_len":512}
```

kevin: Confirming — infra noticed us-west pools are running CUDA 12.1 / driver 535 while us-east pools are still on CUDA 11.8 / driver 520. Our fused attention kernels were built against 11.x, so auto detects incompatibility and falls back. That explains the ~5x p95 tail. Two short fixes: force kernel=prefer_fused (if available) or rebuild fused kernels for 12.x.

ana: (typo fix) I mean ana — I can rerun with kernel=prefer_fused and also disable edge routing (route->nearest only) to see if the edge proxy is amplifying tails. Want to isolate kernel vs edge. maya, want me to run? :rocket:

maya: Yes please. Run two variants: 1) kernel=prefer_fused + edge routing ON, 2) kernel=prefer_fused + edge routing OFF (nearest-only).

benchbot: AUTO-BENCH REPORT (rerun 1769876700)
variant A: kernel=prefer_fused, edge=ON
- us-east1 (A100): 115ms / 210ms / 16ms
- us-west2 (A100): 125ms / 250ms / 28ms  <-- big improvement vs 720ms
- eu-west1 (H100): 92ms / 200ms / 20ms

variant B: kernel=prefer_fused, edge=OFF (nearest-only routing)
- us-east1 (A100): 118ms / 215ms / 17ms
- us-west2 (A100): 120ms / 240ms / 25ms
- eu-west1 (H100): 94ms / 205ms / 21ms

Quick takeaway: forcing fused kernels removes the huge tail in us-west. Turning edge routing off has minor additional improvement (~10ms p95) but the bulk of the regression was kernel fallback.

jorge: Nice — so root cause = kernel compatibility + fallback to slower kernels, edge routing amplified but was not primary.

kevin: Action items I propose:
- schedule kernel rebuild of fused attention for CUDA 12.x on us-west nodes (infra ticket created)
- add a pre-deploy check that verifies fused kernel availability for target driver
- modify edge routing policy to include recent tail-latency metric as a routing dimension (prefer local if tail above threshold)

sre-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: correlated p95 spike window 1769876543–1769876700. Affected: Dedicated workloads on us-west pool. Temporary mitigation: force kernel=prefer_fused where available and scale us-west pool by +25% capacity.

maya: I'll coordinate with infra to roll the kernel rebuild and with product to test canary. Also updating the model onboarding checklist to include a kernel compatibility step for quantized models (especially fused kernels). Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
